summary: Registered secrets are masked on screen, in log_path, callbacks and module logs; register_secret and mask_secrets filters are added; no_log options keep their real value in results instead of VALUE_SPECIFIED_IN_NO_LOG_PARAMETER; short secrets may mask unrelated text.
questions: How do I register my own value as a secret in a playbook?
Why is a short password masking parts of other words?
How do I redact secrets from a string in Jinja?
Why does register_secret fail on an empty value?

answer_card.title: How secret masking affects playbooks
answer_card.answer_md:
Registered secrets are replaced with `$REDACTED$` on screen, in the `log_path` file, in callback output and in module logs on managed nodes. The values remain usable by tasks.

- **`register_secret`** filter: register your own value as a secret.
- **`mask_secrets`** filter: redact registered secrets from a string.

`no_log: true` options are **no longer replaced** with `VALUE_SPECIFIED_IN_NO_LOG_PARAMETER` in results; the real value is kept and registered as a secret. Update playbooks that compared against that placeholder.

A `no_log` value is now masked wherever it appears later. Very short values (one or two characters) get masked inside unrelated words, which hurts readability and can hint at the value.

`register_secret` fails on non-strings or values empty after trimming whitespace; set `validation_action: warn` or `ignore` to return the value unregistered instead.
